issue.body:
Closes #4570

## Description

This PR fixes the tags picker so selecting a suggested tag clears the search input and resets the search state immediately. That keeps stale suggestions from remaining visible after a tag is added and makes repeated tag selection feel consistent.

It also adds widget test coverage for the suggestion-tap flow, verifying that tapping a suggested tag clears the text field and updates the UI as expected.

comment.body: Good catch. Added a new `TagsPickerSearchReset` event (no transformer → synchronous) and a corresponding `_onSearchReset` handler in the bloc that immediately emits `status: initial, query: '', suggestions: []`. `_resetSearchInput` now dispatches that event before clearing the controller, so the suggestion pane collapses in the same frame the tag is committed. The subsequent debounced `TagsPickerQueryChanged('')` that fires when the controller clears becomes a no-op once the query is already `''`.

Tightened the assertions to pin the immediate post-tap state before the debounce window opens. After the single `tester.pump()` the test now also asserts `find.text('mus'), findsNothing` — the key distinction: before the fix, `_onTagsAdded` left `state.query == 'mus'` intact, so `canAddQuery` was still true and a `_SuggestionChip('mus')` remained visible even though 'music' had just been committed. That chip must be gone immediately, not after 300 ms. `find.text('music'), findsOneWidget` stays to confirm the selected chip is present, and the 400 ms pump is kept as a smoke-test that the debounce path also settles cleanly.

issue.body:
### What would you like?

----------------------------------------------

Culturalarchiveera, May 19, 2026, 09:16

Hi Divine Team,

I hope this finds you well.

My name is Skye Laurent, and I’m reaching out on behalf of **CAE aka Cultural Archive Era**, an invite-only cultural preservation event taking place **July 18, 2026** in Los Angeles.

CAE was created to bring back the feeling of the internet before everything became overly polished, overly produced, and overly algorithmic. It is a love letter to the 2014–2018 era of culture, the house parties, the chaos, the music, the creators, the “you had to be there” moments, and most importantly, the platforms that made internet culture feel human.

That is why Divine feels like such an important potential partner for this event.

Before there were “influencers,” there were **Viners**. Before short-form content became an industry, Vine made it a language. Six seconds changed entertainment, comedy, music discovery, fashion, friendship groups, and the way an entire generation learned to create. Vine did not just give people a platform, it gave the world a new kind of star. So many of the creators we now call household names, influencers, and cultural tastemakers were born from that app.

In many ways, Vine was the blueprint.

And now, with Divine bringing that spirit back in a way that feels human-first, creator-first, and refreshingly anti-AI-slop, the timing feels almost too perfect.

CAE is happening in 2026, exactly ten years after 2016, a year that defined an entire internet generation. Our event is designed to feel like stepping back into that moment, but through a modern lens: raw content, real creators, nostalgia-driven storytelling, anonymous “Gossip Girl meets underground rager” marketing, paparazzi-style teasers, viral clue drops, private LA estate energy, and an invite-only guest list curated around people who actually shaped culture.

We are expecting **500 confirmed invite-only guests**, including **A-list celebrities, A-list DJs, legacy creators, tastemakers, press, influencers, and cultural insiders**. Press and marketing begin in **June 2026**, and the campaign is already being built around suspense, nostalgia, secrecy, and community participation.

We would love to explore a partnership where **Divine is featured as an official partner/sponsor of CAE**, with CAE donating a portion of event sales back to Divine in exchange for support, alignment, and platform backing.

This could include:

**Divine x CAE Official Partnership Placement**
Divine featured across our event deck, website, sponsor materials, press language, and social rollout.

**Dedicated “Six-Second Archive” Campaign**
A branded challenge encouraging guests, creators, and fans to post six-second CAE-inspired videos in the spirit of Vine, raw, funny, nostalgic, and human.

**On-Site Divine Content Moment**
A designated “Divine Booth” or content zone where attendees create six-second clips during the event, giving Divine organic celebrity and creator-driven content from the night.

**Nostalgia-Driven PR Angle**
CAE and Divine together tell a bigger story: the return of human-first internet culture, the people who built the creator era, and the platforms that made it possible.

**Founder/Event Legacy Tie-In**
The creators and event coordinators behind the early social-media music festival movement for kids and teens are back, now coming together to create a monumental cultural archive event for the generation that grew up online.

**Social + Press Amplification**
Divine would be included in our June/July marketing rollout across press, influencer content, sponsor announcements, creator storytelling, short-form campaigns, and post-event recap assets.

The benefit for Divine is bigger than logo placement. This is an opportunity to place Divine directly inside the cultural conversation it was built to reclaim.

CAE is not just an event. It is a moment for the internet to remember what it felt like when content was fun, strange, unfiltered, and made by real people. Divine represents that same energy. It is not just bringing back Vine, it is bringing back the feeling of wanting to create because it was funny, because it was weird, because your friends would get it, and because six seconds could change everything.

We believe Divine should be part of CAE because Vine helped create the very culture CAE is preserving.

This is not just sponsorship. It is a full-circle cultural collaboration.

We would love to schedule a call with your team to discuss how we can structure the partnership, including the donation percentage from CAE sales, brand placement, content activations, and how Divine can be meaningfully integrated into the event experience.

Thank you for rebuilding something the internet never really stopped missing.

comment.body: Thanks for reporting! Your logs confirm a known service-initialization race condition during app startup. We are tracking the fix for this in our primary tracker: #3923. I am closing this to consolidate your report there.

review.body: This is close, but I don't think the fix fully lands yet. The widget now clears the controller value, but the search state still resets through the debounced query path, so stale results can remain visible briefly after a suggestion tap. The new test also doesn't prove that behavior is fixed because it can pass with `music` rendered only as the selected chip. Please make the search-state reset immediate on commit and tighten the test to assert the suggestion/empty-results UI disappears right away.

comment.body: This assertion doesn't verify that the stale suggestion UI was cleared. `find.text('music')` will also match the selected tag chip, so the test still passes if the old suggestion/result state lingers. It would be stronger to assert the immediate post-tap state directly: empty controller, no suggestion chip, and no transient `No results` pane from the previous query.

Clearing the `TextEditingValue` here only updates the controller. The actual query/suggestions reset still depends on the debounced `TagsPickerQueryChanged('')` path, so the previous results can remain on screen briefly after a suggestion tap. If the goal is an immediate reset, that state transition needs to happen synchronously when a tag is committed instead of waiting for the debounce window.

issue.title: feat(notifications): mark all as read when leaving the screen

labels.name: needs-issue
labels.description: PR needs a linked tracking issue

issue.body:
## Summary

- When the user opens notifications (either the standalone `/notifications` route or the Notifications segment inside the inbox) and then leaves, every visible notification is flipped to read and the badge collapses to 0.
- Triggers: bottom-nav tab switch (ShellRoute unmount), Messages/Notifications segment toggle inside `InboxView` (KeyedSubtree swap), and auth flip (pubkey-keyed subtree remount).
- The badge stays at 0 until a genuinely new unread notification arrives — either pushed live via `acceptRealtime` or returned as unread by the next `refresh()`. No change needed on the badge side: `watchUnreadCount()` is already derived from the snapshot.

## Implementation

A small `MarkAllReadOnDispose` stateful wrapper fires `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` once in `dispose()`. The repository already does the optimistic snapshot flip + server write + rollback on failure (the PR #4034 semantics), so the badge cubit and feed bloc recover consistently if the API call fails.

- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose.dart` *(new)* — the wrapper.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/widgets.dart` — export it.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_page.dart` — wrap `NotificationsView`.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page.dart` — wrap `_InboxNotificationsScaffold`.

### Why a wrapper instead of a bloc event

The repository's `markAllAsRead()` must outlive the `BlocProvider` being torn down with the route. The repository instance is owned higher up (Riverpod), so dispatching a bloc event in `dispose` would race the bloc's own close. Calling the repository directly from the wrapper sidesteps that.

### Why dispose-on-leave and not on-open

Mark-on-open would hide brand-new notifications the user hadn't actually seen yet (e.g. a relay arrival in the same frame as the open). The existing `notifications_page_test.dart` "does not mark notifications read on open" assertion still pins that contract — only the dispose path was added.

### Shell architecture note

I verified `app_router.dart` uses a plain `ShellRoute`, not `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack`. That means tab switches via the bottom nav *do* unmount the previous tab's subtree, so `dispose()` is the right trigger. If we later migrate to `StatefulShellRoute`, this would need to be re-wired to a route listener.

labels.name: needs-issue

issue.body:
## Summary

- When the user opens notifications (either the standalone `/notifications` route or the Notifications segment inside the inbox) and then leaves, every visible notification is flipped to read and the badge collapses to 0.
- Triggers: bottom-nav tab switch (ShellRoute unmount), Messages/Notifications segment toggle inside `InboxView` (KeyedSubtree swap), and auth flip (pubkey-keyed subtree remount).
- The badge stays at 0 until a genuinely new unread notification arrives — either pushed live via `acceptRealtime` or returned as unread by the next `refresh()`. No change needed on the badge side: `watchUnreadCount()` is already derived from the snapshot.

## Implementation

A small `MarkAllReadOnDispose` stateful wrapper fires `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` once in `dispose()`. The repository already does the optimistic snapshot flip + server write + rollback on failure (the PR #4034 semantics), so the badge cubit and feed bloc recover consistently if the API call fails.

- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose.dart` *(new)* — the wrapper.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/widgets.dart` — export it.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_page.dart` — wrap `NotificationsView`.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page.dart` — wrap `_InboxNotificationsScaffold`.

### Why a wrapper instead of a bloc event

The repository's `markAllAsRead()` must outlive the `BlocProvider` being torn down with the route. The repository instance is owned higher up (Riverpod), so dispatching a bloc event in `dispose` would race the bloc's own close. Calling the repository directly from the wrapper sidesteps that.

### Why dispose-on-leave and not on-open

Mark-on-open would hide brand-new notifications the user hadn't actually seen yet (e.g. a relay arrival in the same frame as the open). The existing `notifications_page_test.dart` "does not mark notifications read on open" assertion still pins that contract — only the dispose path was added.

### Shell architecture note

I verified `app_router.dart` uses a plain `ShellRoute`, not `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack`. That means tab switches via the bottom nav *do* unmount the previous tab's subtree, so `dispose()` is the right trigger. If we later migrate to `StatefulShellRoute`, this would need to be re-wired to a route listener.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib/notifications test/notifications` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications/view/notifications_page_test.dart test/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page_test.dart test/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose_test.dart` — 19/19 pass
- [x] New `MarkAllReadOnDispose` widget tests cover mounted-no-call, unmount-calls-once, error-swallowing, and child rendering
- [x] New "marks all notifications read when the page is unmounted" test on both `NotificationsPage` and `InboxNotificationsPage`
- [x] Existing "does not mark on open" + "does not fan out across the five filter tabs" assertions still pass
- [ ] Manual: open inbox → notifications segment → tap home → return to inbox → notifications badge should be 0, list rows show read styling
- [ ] Manual: open notifications → background app → foreground → badge state preserved (dispose did not fire)
- [ ] Manual: receive a new like/comment via WS while away from notifications → badge bumps to 1

comment.body:
Pushed `3e35c48` — the three-layer mark-read fix that explains the "zombie badge" you saw on the first build.

The on-leave dispose hook from the first commit was firing correctly; the badge bounced because the underlying `markNotificationsRead` call has been broken since #4271. Three independent bugs were combining on every POST to `/api/users/{pubkey}/notifications/read`:

1. **Response shape mismatch (`MarkReadResponse.fromJson`)** — the funnelcake server returns `{"marked_count": N, "marked_all": bool}` (no `success` field), but the model defaulted `success` to `false` when absent. Every successful 200 was misread as a soft-failure, the client threw, and the repository's `catch` rolled back the optimistic flip. Existing tests passed because the fixtures synthetically sent `{"success": true, ...}` — which never matched production traffic.

2. **NIP-98 `URL mismatch` (`notification_repository_provider`)** — the auth callback was signing the *path* (`/api/users/.../notifications/read`) while the request went to the *full URL* (`https://api.divine.video/...`). Added `FunnelcakeApiClient.notificationsReadUri()` so the repository signs the same URL it posts to.

3. **NIP-98 `payload hash mismatch`** — the callback was never given the request body, so `nip98_auth_service` hashed `""` while the actual body was `{}` or `{"notification_ids": [...]}`. Threaded a `body` parameter through the `AuthHeadersProvider` typedef → repository call sites → provider wiring → `createAuthToken(payload: body)`. The new `FunnelcakeApiClient.buildMarkNotificationsReadBody()` static helper produces the body in one place so the repo and the client can't drift.

Each bug independently caused the rollback; all three had to be fixed to make the badge stay at 0. The on-leave dispose just made the failure visible every time you tabbed away.

Tests: 281 / 281 pass locally (`flutter test packages/funnelcake_api_client packages/notification_repository test/notifications`).

issue.title: fix(macos): use data protection keychain to stop repeated keychain prompts
issue.body:
Closes #4575

## Summary

- Removes the explicit `useDataProtectionKeyChain: false` override on `MacOsOptions` in `flutterSecureStorageProvider`. The flutter_secure_storage default is now `true`, which uses the modern data protection keychain.
- Items are scoped to the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement (already configured in `DebugProfile.entitlements` and `Release.entitlements` as `\$(AppIdentifierPrefix)\$(CFBundleIdentifier)`) instead of the binary's code signature. Rebuilds no longer trigger the "enter your login keychain password" prompt for every stored item on every fresh build.

## Why

Every `flutter run` / fresh macOS build produces a new code signature. The legacy login keychain scopes ACLs to that signature, so the user gets prompted once per stored item (auth token, nostr key, OAuth tokens, pubkey cache, …) on every rebuild. "Always Allow" only sticks for a single signature. The data protection keychain uses the `keychain-access-groups` entitlement instead, which is stable across signatures.

## Tradeoff

Existing macOS users have credentials in the legacy login keychain. After this change the app reads the data protection keychain and won't find them, so they'll need to sign in again on macOS. iOS, Android, and Linux are unaffected.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh `flutter run -d macos` no longer prompts for the login keychain password.
- [ ] Sign in, quit, rebuild, relaunch → still signed in, no keychain prompt.
- [ ] On the first run after the upgrade, the user is prompted to sign in again (expected — see Tradeoff).

issue.title: feat(notifications): mark all as read when leaving the screen

labels.name: needs-issue
labels.description: PR needs a linked tracking issue

issue.body:
## Summary

- When the user opens notifications (either the standalone `/notifications` route or the Notifications segment inside the inbox) and then leaves, every visible notification is flipped to read and the badge collapses to 0.
- Triggers: bottom-nav tab switch (ShellRoute unmount), Messages/Notifications segment toggle inside `InboxView` (KeyedSubtree swap), and auth flip (pubkey-keyed subtree remount).
- The badge stays at 0 until a genuinely new unread notification arrives — either pushed live via `acceptRealtime` or returned as unread by the next `refresh()`. No change needed on the badge side: `watchUnreadCount()` is already derived from the snapshot.

## Implementation

A small `MarkAllReadOnDispose` stateful wrapper fires `NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead()` once in `dispose()`. The repository already does the optimistic snapshot flip + server write + rollback on failure (the PR #4034 semantics), so the badge cubit and feed bloc recover consistently if the API call fails.

- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose.dart` *(new)* — the wrapper.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/widgets/widgets.dart` — export it.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_page.dart` — wrap `NotificationsView`.
- `mobile/lib/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page.dart` — wrap `_InboxNotificationsScaffold`.

### Why a wrapper instead of a bloc event

The repository's `markAllAsRead()` must outlive the `BlocProvider` being torn down with the route. The repository instance is owned higher up (Riverpod), so dispatching a bloc event in `dispose` would race the bloc's own close. Calling the repository directly from the wrapper sidesteps that.

### Why dispose-on-leave and not on-open

Mark-on-open would hide brand-new notifications the user hadn't actually seen yet (e.g. a relay arrival in the same frame as the open). The existing `notifications_page_test.dart` "does not mark notifications read on open" assertion still pins that contract — only the dispose path was added.

### Shell architecture note

I verified `app_router.dart` uses a plain `ShellRoute`, not `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack`. That means tab switches via the bottom nav *do* unmount the previous tab's subtree, so `dispose()` is the right trigger. If we later migrate to `StatefulShellRoute`, this would need to be re-wired to a route listener.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter analyze lib/notifications test/notifications` — clean
- [x] `flutter test test/notifications/view/notifications_page_test.dart test/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page_test.dart test/notifications/widgets/mark_all_read_on_dispose_test.dart` — 19/19 pass
- [x] New `MarkAllReadOnDispose` widget tests cover mounted-no-call, unmount-calls-once, error-swallowing, and child rendering
- [x] New "marks all notifications read when the page is unmounted" test on both `NotificationsPage` and `InboxNotificationsPage`
- [x] Existing "does not mark on open" + "does not fan out across the five filter tabs" assertions still pass
- [ ] Manual: open inbox → notifications segment → tap home → return to inbox → notifications badge should be 0, list rows show read styling
- [ ] Manual: open notifications → background app → foreground → badge state preserved (dispose did not fire)
- [ ] Manual: receive a new like/comment via WS while away from notifications → badge bumps to 1

issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows the video editor sometimes passing a local extracted audio path into the remote-audio loading path.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue e81e2bc1d6713fa5d91e7b15a0950e18: 16 nonfatal events, 2 users.
- Error: Invalid argument(s): No host specified in URI /var/mobile/.../extracted_audio_*.wav.
- Stack: _HttpClient.getUrl -> AudioClipPlayer._defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader -> AudioClipPlayer.setClip -> AudioTimingCubit._setClippedAudioSource -> AudioTimingCubit.resumePlayback -> VideoAudioEditorTimingScreen fling handler.
- Code: mobile/lib/blocs/video_editor/audio_timing/audio_timing_cubit.dart builds AudioSourceConfig.network(...) for non-bundled editor audio around lines 216-230.
- Code: mobile/packages/sound_service/lib/src/audio_clip_player.dart only uses local-file handling when config.isFile is true; otherwise it sends the URI to HttpClient.

This is app-owned: a local iOS file path should never reach the network loader.

Acceptance criteria:
- Local absolute paths and file:// URIs produced by editor extraction go through AudioSourceConfig.file.
- Remote audio loading rejects or records a controlled error for non-http(s) URIs without calling HttpClient.openUrl.
- Add focused tests for AudioTimingCubit source selection and AudioClipPlayer URI classification.
- Preserve existing behavior for bundled assets and real http/https remote sounds.

review.body:
Re-review of `5a4a62d30` + `82d0cd82f` — all three prior blockers resolved.

**Riverpod → BLoC migration ✓.** `mobile/lib/blocs/sound_library/sound_library_bloc.dart` ships `SoundLibraryBloc` with sealed events, enum-status state (`SoundLibraryProvidersStatus`, `SoundLibrarySearchStatus`), `restartable()` on `QueryChanged`, `droppable()` on `PageRequested`, errors via `addError()` (no error strings/exceptions in state), no mutable instance vars. Old Riverpod hooks fully removed.

**Composition moved to repository ✓.** `SoundLibraryApiClient` now lives in `mobile/packages/sounds_repository/lib/src/sound_library_api_client.dart` (Flutter-free: `http` + `meta` only). `SoundsRepository.fetchExternalProviders()` and `.searchExternalLibrary(SoundLibrarySearchRequest)` are the BLoC's only surface — client is internal, matching `architecture.md`.

**`_soundFromJson` hardened ✓.** New `_requireString` helper throws `SoundLibraryApiException`; the `AudioLicenseMetadata.fromJson` `TypeError` is caught and rewrapped with a single annotated `// ignore: avoid_catching_errors`. Regression test added.

**Forward-looking concerns (non-blocking):**
- When the UI PR lands, the consuming widget must `ref.watch(soundsRepositoryProvider)` and put it in a `ValueKey` on `BlocProvider<SoundLibraryBloc>` per `state_management.md` "Bridging Riverpod-provided dependencies into BlocProvider." Worth pinning in the design doc.
- `pubkey: AudioEvent.externalProviderMarker` ('external_provider') stuffs a sentinel into a Nostr-pubkey field — anything calling `npub.encode(pubkey)` will choke. Cleaner shape would be a nullable `pubkey` or an `origin` enum. Flag before any UI reads `pubkey` of external sounds.
- Formatter churn in 6 unrelated `models/` files (from pinning Flutter 3.41.9) is mechanically correct but ideally would be a separate `chore(models)` PR per `code_style.md` "PR Scope". Acceptable here since the pin lives in this PR.

CI green, `sounds_repository` at 100% coverage. Verdict: LGTM (posted as comment — GitHub blocks `--approve` on own PRs).

I tested it and everything works well. I left a few comments, but nothing blocking.

@Chardot, this change affects the design, so it’s something you should be aware so we can improve that part later as well.

Re-review after `5f40dd11` ("fix(library): drop confirm dialog, wire undo snackbar, show purge countdown").

## Prior findings — resolution

| # | Finding | Status |
|---|---------|--------|
| 1 | Library delete dialog said "permanently removed" but soft-deleted | **Resolved**. Confirm dialogs removed from both single (`clips_tab.dart` `_softDeleteClip`) and batch (`library_screen.dart`) paths. Orphan `libraryDeleteClip*` keys removed from `app_en.arb`. |
| 2 | `lastDeletedClipIds` populated but unconsumed | **Resolved**. `BlocListener` in `library_screen.dart:424` triggers a snackbar with Undo on `lastDeletedCount` transitions, dispatching `ClipsLibraryRestoreClips(deletedIds)`. The pre-emit `clearDeletedCount: true` in both single- and batch-delete handlers correctly drives `N → null → M` so consecutive deletes of the same size still refire. |
| 3 | Trash UI showed `recordedAt`, no purge countdown | **Resolved**. `DivineVideoClip.deletedAt` plumbed from `clips.deleted_at`. `_daysUntilPurge` derives from `deletedAt + ClipLibraryService.trashRetention`. Countdown renders via `libraryTrashAutoDeletes` ICU plural (today / tomorrow / in N days). Retention constant lives on the service — purge sweep and UI countdown share one source of truth. |
| 4a | Best-effort purge not wrapped in try/catch | **Resolved**. `app_lifecycle_handler.dart:68` now wraps `purgeExpiredTrash` in try/catch with a logged failure path. |
| 4b | No-op onTap/onLongPress on trash thumbnail | **Resolved**. `VideoClipThumbnailCard.onTap/onLongPress` made nullable (`VoidCallback?`); trash tile passes neither. |
| 4c | Invariant test: `recoverMissingAssets` can't resurrect trashed | **Indirect coverage only**. No explicit test, but the guarantee follows structurally: `recoverMissingAssets(List<DivineVideoClip>)` operates on the parameter; trashed rows never reach it because `getLibraryClips` / `getAllClips` / `watchLibraryClips` / `getClipsByDraftId` all filter `deleted_at IS NULL` (verified in `clips_dao.dart`). One dedicated test would still be cheap insurance — not a blocker. |

## New observations on this revision

1. **`libraryClipsDeletedUndoLabel` and `libraryTrashAutoDeletes` are English-only + allowlisted.** The other 6 library-trash keys + `videoRecorderClipUndoLabel` and the rewritten `videoRecorderClipDeletedMessage` ARE translated across all 17 locales (`631ea01d`). Mixed approach — fine per the documented allowlist policy, but worth a follow-up to translate these two as well so the snackbar Undo and the countdown match the rest of the surface.

2. **`_daysUntilPurge` returns 0 for `deletedAt == null`.** The comment frames it as "a degraded row state — surface as 'today' rather than crashing". That's safe but slightly misleading — a clip with `deletedAt == null` should not be in `getTrashedClips()` (DAO filter is `deletedAt IS NOT NULL`). Worth either an `assert(clip.deletedAt != null)` to catch programming errors, or trusting the DAO contract and dropping the null branch. Minor.

3. **Schema migration safety.** `_addColumnIfMissing('clips', 'deleted_at', 'INTEGER')` plus `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent and tolerates re-runs. `schemaVersion` stays at 1, so existing installs hit the ADD COLUMN on first launch via the migration step. Reads with the new `deletedAt IS NULL` filter will treat all pre-migration rows as active (NULL = active), which is correct. No data migration needed.

4. **Cross-device sync is out of scope.** Trash is local-only — deleting on Phone A does not propagate to Phone B's library. The PR is explicit about this being a local recovery feature, not a Nostr-level retraction, so this is acknowledged scope, not a gap.

5. **Test coverage** for the new service surface (softDelete, restore, hardDelete, purgeExpiredTrash) is solid in `clip_library_service_test.dart`. Bloc tests cover the new events. No tests for the trash *screen* itself (`library_trash_screen.dart`) — adding one widget test for the countdown rendering and Restore/Delete-now button wiring would close that gap.

## Verdict

**Approve.** All four prior findings addressed cleanly. The two open items (translation of the two self-review-pass keys, trash screen widget test) are minor follow-ups rather than blockers. Schema migration is safe, snackbar undo race-condition is handled via the pre-emit null-clear, and the retention constant is correctly centralized.

## Re-review of c8dffad1: refactor(audio): extract _configForUrl helper

### Verdict: Approve (re-approve)

Pure code-organization refactor on top of the already-approved fix. No behavior change, all prior correctness guarantees preserved.

### What c8dffad1 actually does

Two changes, both non-functional:

1. **`audio_timing_cubit.dart`** — extracts the inline URL-classification block from `_setClippedAudioSource` into a `static AudioSourceConfig _configForUrl(String url, {required Duration start, required Duration end})` helper. Byte-for-byte identical predicate (`parsed == null || parsed.scheme.isEmpty || parsed.scheme == 'file' || url.startsWith('/')`), identical `Uri.toFilePath()` decoding path, identical fallback to `AudioSourceConfig.network`.
2. **`audio_clip_player.dart`** — appends one sentence to the guard's leading comment noting that Android `content://` and web `blob:` are rejected by the same scheme check.

That's it. git diff between 3c771d2 and c8dffad1 touches exactly two files; no test files changed.

### Correctness preservation

- **Logic equivalence:** byte-for-byte same predicate and decoding. Only naming change is `uri` -> `url` parameter; the predicate uses both parsed `Uri?` and raw string identically. The `parsed.scheme == 'file' ? parsed.toFilePath() : url` branch matches the prior inline form exactly.
- **Three-way classification** still lives at the right layer (the cubit that knows the `AudioEvent` contract). Bundled-asset branch is untouched and still constructed inline above the helper call — appropriate, since asset routing needs `_sound.assetPath` and a different config constructor.
- **Defense-in-depth boundary** in `AudioClipPlayer._defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader` is unchanged; the doc comment addition is documentation-only and accurate (`content://` and `blob:` both have non-http(s) schemes and will hit the `ArgumentError` branch).

### Test coverage still binds the behavior

The four `blocTest`s in `audio_timing_cubit_test.dart` (bare path -> `.file`, `file://` -> `.file`, https -> `.network`, bundled -> `.asset`) exercise the same observable contract via `cubit.resumePlayback()` and the captured `setClip` argument. They route through `_setClippedAudioSource` which now calls `_configForUrl`, so the helper is covered transitively. No separate helper-level unit test was added; given the integration-level coverage exercises the same four branches, that's reasonable.

The two `audio_clip_player_test.dart` regressions (guard throws on non-http(s); `.file` skips the remote loader) still anchor the player-layer contract — the doc comment change cannot affect them.

### Conventions

- Private `static` helper with focused dartdoc explaining the supported / unsupported scheme matrix — matches `code_style.md` (comment the *why*: the unsupported-scheme fallthrough is intentional and traceable to the defense-in-depth `ArgumentError`).
- Helper is at the right granularity: takes only `url`, `start`, `end`; returns the typed config. Not over-extracted.
- No `// TODO`, no skipped tests, no behavior shift, no scope creep.

### Risk

Zero net new risk. Refactor reduces the cyclomatic complexity of `_setClippedAudioSource` and makes the doc comment trail (cubit dartdoc -> player guard comment) align across both layers about which schemes are in vs out of scope. Re-approving.

issue.title: chore(notifications): tighten badge a11y/theming and drop dead code
issue.body:
Closes #4559

## Summary
Close out small residual debt in the notifications subtree as part of epic #4200:

- Replace inline `TextStyle(fontSize: 11, fontWeight: bold)` with `VineTheme.labelSmallFont()` and `Icon(Icons.circle)` with a plain `Container(BoxShape.circle)` so the badge stops abusing the icon font for a geometric primitive (`ui_theming.md`).
- Wrap both badge variants in `Semantics(label, container: true)` reading the new pluralised `notificationsBadgeUnread` ARB key so screen readers announce the unread count (`accessibility.md`).
- Isolate the `AnimatedNotificationBadge` pulse animation under a `RepaintBoundary` to keep its repaints from cascading into the parent nav icon (`performance.md`).
- Delete the unused `filterRealtimeNotification` helper on `NotificationRepository` (zero callers in `lib/`, `packages/`, `test/`). Realtime blocked-actor filtering still runs via `acceptRealtime` → `_enrichAndGroup` → `_applyBlockFilter`.
- Delete the legacy `event_handlers_simple_test.dart` file — a group-level `skip: true` masked 6 already-skipped tests, and the same behaviour is covered by `notification_repository_test.dart` after the WS bridge migration in #4288.

Notification subtree skipped-test count: 6 → 0.

## Test plan
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test` — `No issues found!`

- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/ test/notifications/ test/blocs/notifications/ test/router/app_shell_notification_badge_test.dart test/screens/inbox/` — 2345 tests pass.

issue.title: fix: audio progressively gets louder during iOS recording after using countdown feature
issue.body:
## Summary
On iOS, the audio recorded during a video recording session gradually increases in volume over time. The issue appears to be triggered specifically when the countdown feature is used before starting the recording.

## Environment
- Platform: iOS
- Feature involved: Camera countdown

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open the camera screen
2. Enable / use the countdown feature to start a recording
3. Record a video with audio
4. Play back the recorded video

## Actual Result
The audio volume progressively increases throughout the recording — the longer the recording, the louder the audio becomes.

## Expected Result
Audio volume should remain consistent and stable throughout the entire recording session.
